Latin.note: The Latin starts with the surviving invitation to offer the sacrifices. The Greek opening directions about custody, bowing and keeping clean are compressed or not separately expressed in this reviewed Latin paragraph. The section has surviving correspondence; no wording has been reconstructed.
The Latin starts with the identifiable gifts sent to Eleazar. The Greek introductory resumption of the preceding gifts has no distinct counterpart here. The surviving Latin wording is preserved.

The three-year duration attached in Greek XII.143 to the total exemption is expressed in the following Latin interval, XII.144, with the third-part relief. The transmitted Latin syntax and order are preserved.
The Latin attaches the three-year duration to the third-part relief here. In Greek the duration belongs to XII.143's preceding total exemption. No text has been moved or corrected.

The dating material corresponding to Greek XII.248 (Olympiad 153, day 25 and the named month) occurs here in Latin paragraph latin-book12-num246, before “Capit eam sine conflictione”. The Latin attaches it to the first capture. See XII.248 for the displaced correspondence.

This Latin interval contains the opening counterpart of Greek XII.247. Its ending, “multasque abeo auferens pecunias ad antiochiam reuersus est”, resumes later within the Latin interval displayed at XII.249. The transmitted order is preserved.

No independent Latin interval. Dating material corresponding to this Greek section survives earlier within XII.246, in latin-book12-num246: “centesima quinquagesima tertia olimpiade. uicesimo et quinto mensis chasleu quem mache dones appelleon nominant.” This is displaced correspondence. The distinct second-capture notice has no identifiable counterpart in the reviewed Latin context. Greek and English remain independently accessible.

Partial and reordered correspondence. The opening clause “nec non etiam eos qui portas aperientes ciuitatem ei tradiderunt propter templi diuitias interficit” corresponds to Greek XII.249. The following “multasque abeo auferens pecunias ad antiochiam reuersus est” resumes Greek XII.247. The entire displayed Latin interval does not correspond exclusively to Greek XII.249; the transmitted order is preserved.

The Latin starts with Mathathias' refusal. The preliminary Greek promise of public example and royal honour is compressed in this transcription. The surviving refusal and its continuation are retained.

The closing Latin arrival and loss of troops continue into material corresponding to the opening of Greek XII.356. XII.356's independent Latin interval begins with the subsequent report. No text has been moved.

The Latin arrival and loss of troops corresponding to the opening of Greek XII.356 are expressed at the end of the preceding interval, XII.355. This selection starts with the new report, “quidam ei nuntiauit”. The transmitted order is preserved.
The Greek injunction to conceal the news about Philip is repeated later in the transmitted Latin, within the interval displayed at XII.381. The original order and repetition are preserved.

This Latin interval includes the resumed injunction to conceal Philip corresponding to Greek XII.380, before the final assent. Its entire wording does not correspond exclusively to Greek XII.381; transmitted order is preserved.

The Latin assurances and their scope here compress material also belonging to the opening of Greek XII.396. The independent Latin interval at XII.396 starts with Bachides' subsequent breach. The original wording is preserved.

This Latin selection begins with the surviving breach by Bachides. The Greek opening oath-taking has no separate Latin clause; the assurances and same-party scope are compressed within the preceding interval, XII.395. No whole-section absence is claimed.

The Latin preserves Judas' resolve to fight even if death follows. The Greek closing contrast between glory and flight and the author's summary of the speech have no separately identifiable Latin clauses in the reviewed context. The surviving interval remains selectable; the cause of the difference is unknown.
